meanings.usage: 指使人发笑的戏剧或表演形式
常与up连用，表示排队等候
用于表达令人失望或糟糕的情况
形容缺乏趣味或刺激的事物
指专业表演者，如歌手、舞者等
用于强调某事清晰可见或毋庸置疑
描述人因紧张而感到不安的状态
形容动作不自然或不熟练
用于扩大声音的电子设备
fail to do something表示未能做成某事
表示不确定的较小数量
对女性听众或观众的正式称呼

examples.en: When the news got round, everyone came to see.
examples.zh: 消息传开后，大家都来看了。

examples.en: We had to queue for hours to get in.
examples.zh: 我们不得不排了好几个小时的队才能进去。

examples.en: As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out laughing.
examples.zh: 他一开口，大家就突然大笑起来。

examples.en: He stood awkwardly before the microphone.
examples.zh: 他尴尬地站在麦克风前。

examples.en: He spoke at the beginning of the programme.
Those who failed to get in need not have felt disappointed.
examples.zh: 那些没能进去的人不必感到失望。

examples.en: Many of the artistes who should have appeared did not come.
examples.zh: 许多本应该出现的艺人没有来。

examples.en: Those who failed to get in need not have felt disappointed.
examples.zh: 那些没能进去的人本不必感到失望。

examples.en: As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out laughing.
examples.zh: 他一开口，大家就大笑起来。

phrases.usage: 女士们，晚上好（的错误说法）

examples.en: What he actually said was: 'Good ladies, evening and gentlemen!'
examples.zh: 他实际说的是：'女士们好，晚上和先生们！'

grammar.title: 情态动词need的用法（needn't have done）
grammar.structure: 主语 + needn't have + 过去分词
grammar.definition: needn't have + 过去分词表示本不必做某事（但实际上已经做了） 用于表达某动作是不必要的，但已经发生了

examples.en: Those who failed to get in need not have felt disappointed.
examples.zh: 那些没能进去的人本不必感到失望。

examples.en: You needn't have waited for me.

grammar.title: 情态动词should的用法（should have done）
grammar.structure: 主语 + should have + 过去分词
grammar.definition: should have + 过去分词表示本应该做某事（但实际没做） 用于表达遗憾或责备，暗示期望与现实的差距

examples.en: Many of the artistes who should have appeared did not come.
examples.zh: 许多本应该出现的艺人没有来。

examples.en: I should have studied harder for the exam.
examples.zh: 我本应该更努力学习考试的。

grammar.title: when引导的时间状语从句
grammar.definition: when引导的时间状语从句，说明主句动作发生的背景或时机 when在此处意为'当...的时候'或'当...的消息传开时'

examples.en: When the news got round that a comedy show would be presented, we all rushed to see it.
examples.zh: 当免费喜剧表演的消息传开时，我们都赶去看。

patterns.pattern: People will do anything to + 动词原形

original.en: People will do anything to see a free show--even if it is a bad one.
original.zh: 人们会做任何事去看免费表演——即使是很糟糕的。

imitations.en: People will do anything to get a bargain.
imitations.zh: 人们会做任何事来买到便宜货。

imitations.en: Students will do anything to pass the exam.
imitations.zh: 学生们会做任何事来通过考试。

patterns.pattern: When the news got round that...

original.en: When the news got round that a comedy show would be presented at our local cinema, we all rushed to see it.
original.zh: 当喜剧表演将在当地电影院上演的消息传开时，我们都赶去看。

imitations.en: When the news got round that the store was closing down, everyone rushed there.
imitations.zh: 当那家店即将关门的消息传开时，大家都赶了过去。

imitations.en: When the news got round that he won the lottery, his phone never stopped ringing.
imitations.zh: 当他中彩票的消息传开时，他的电话响个不停。

original.en: The only funny things we heard that evening came from the advertiser.
original.zh: 那天晚上我们听到的唯一有趣的事情来自那个广告商。

imitations.en: The only food left in the fridge was some old bread.
imitations.zh: 冰箱里剩下的唯一食物是一些旧面包。

imitations.en: The only person who understood the problem was the teacher.
imitations.zh: 唯一理解这个问题的人是老师。

patterns.pattern: 主语 + be obviously + 形容词/副词

original.en: He was obviously very nervous and for some minutes stood awkwardly before the microphone.
original.zh: 他显然非常紧张，在麦克风前笨拙地站了好几分钟。

imitations.en: She was obviously very tired after the long journey.
imitations.zh: 长途旅行后，她显然非常疲惫。

imitations.en: The student was obviously very nervous during the presentation.
imitations.zh: 那个学生在做报告时显然非常紧张。

lines.en: People will do anything to see a free show -- even if it is a bad one.
lines.zh: 人们总要想尽办法看不花钱的演出——哪怕是拙劣的演出。

lines.en: When the news got round that a comedy show would be presented at our local cinema by the P. and U.
lines.zh: 当“皮尤”鸟食公司将在我们当地影院演出喜剧节目的消息传开后，我们都赶紧跑去观看。

lines.en: Bird Seed Company, we all rushed to see it.
lines.zh: 我们不得不排了好几个小时才进得场去。

lines.en: We had to queue for hours to get in and there must have been several hundred people present just before the show began.
lines.zh: 在演出开始前场内肯定已有好几百人了。

lines.en: Unfortunately, the show was one of the dullest we have ever seen.
lines.zh: 不幸的是，这次演出是我们看过的最乏味的演出了。

lines.en: Those who failed to get in need not have felt disappointed , as many of the artistes who should have appeared did not come.
lines.zh: 那些没能进到场内的人没有必要感到失望，因为很多应该出场的专业演员都没有来。

lines.en: The only funny things we heard that evening came from the advertiser at the beginning of the programme.
lines.zh: 那天晚上唯一有趣的事情是节目开始时那个报幕员的开场白。

lines.en: He was obviously very nervous and for some minutes stood awkwardly before the microphone .
lines.zh: 他显然非常紧张，局促不安地在麦克风前站了好几分钟。

lines.en: As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out laughing.
lines.zh: 但他刚一开口说话，人们便哄堂大笑起来。

lines.en: We all know what the poor man should have said, but what he actually said was: 'This is the Poo and Ee Seed Bird Company. Good ladies, evening and gentlemen!"
lines.zh: 我们都明白那个可怜的人应该说些什么，而他实际说的却是：“这是‘浦伊’鸟食公司，好女士们，晚上和先生们！”

questions.q: Who made the only funny joke that evening and why?
questions.zh: 那天晚上唯一逗乐大家的人是谁？原因是什么？
questions.a: The advertiser at the beginning of the programme. He was very nervous and made a slip of the tongue: he should have said 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', but what he actually said was 'Good ladies, evening and gentlemen'.
questions.aZh: 是节目开始时那位报幕员。他非常紧张，一时口误：本该说‘女士们、先生们，晚上好’，实际却说成了‘好女士们，晚上和先生们’。
questions.hint: 见课文最后两段：报幕员报公司名时把词序说乱了（burst out laughing 之前）。

questions.q: Why need the people who failed to get in not have felt disappointed?
questions.zh: 那些没能进场的人为什么本不必感到失望？
questions.a: Because many of the artistes who should have appeared did not come, so the show was a poor one anyway.
questions.aZh: 因为很多本该出场的专业演员都没有来，演出本来就很糟，所以没看成也没什么可惜。
questions.hint: 见课文‘Those who failed to get in need not have felt disappointed, as…’一句。

questions.q: What did the audience do as soon as the advertiser opened his mouth?
questions.zh: 报幕员一开口，观众有什么反应？
questions.a: As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out laughing.
questions.aZh: 他刚一开口，所有人便哄堂大笑起来。
questions.hint: 见课文倒数第二段 burst out laughing。

questions.q: What does 'the news got round' mean in the text?
questions.zh: 文中 'the news got round' 是什么意思？
questions.a: It means the news spread and became widely known.
questions.aZh: 意思是消息传开了、传遍了。
questions.hint: 见课文第二句 news got round that…，get round 即消息传播。

questions.q: What makes the advertiser's mistake funny, and what does the text suggest about speaking in public?
questions.zh: 报幕员的错误为什么好笑？课文对‘当众讲话’暗示了什么？
questions.a: Because he mixed up the fixed greeting 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', turning it into a nonsense sentence. It suggests that even a short public announcement needs steady nerves, and that nervousness easily leads to a slip of the tongue.
questions.aZh: 因为他把固定问候语‘Good evening, ladies and gentlemen’的词序打乱，说成了一句不知所云的话。这说明当众讲话需要镇定，紧张很容易造成口误。
questions.hint: 结合课文末句 should have said…but what he actually said… 的对比思考。

translation:
人们总要想尽办法看不花钱的演出——哪怕是拙劣的演出。
当“皮尤”鸟食公司将在我们当地影院演出喜剧节目的消息传开后，我们都赶紧跑去观看。
我们不得不排了好几个小时才进得场去。
在演出开始前场内肯定已有好几百人了。
不幸的是，这次演出是我们看过的最乏味的演出了。
那些没能进到场内的人没有必要感到失望，因为很多应该出场的专业演员都没有来。
那天晚上唯一有趣的事情是节目开始时那个报幕员的开场白。
他显然非常紧张，局促不安地在麦克风前站了好几分钟。
但他刚一开口说话，人们便哄堂大笑起来。
我们都明白那个可怜的人应该说些什么，而他实际说的却是：“这是‘浦伊’鸟食公司，好女士们，晚上和先生们！”
title: A Slip of the Tongue
subtitle: 口误

lead.question: 一台乏味的免费演出，全场唯一的笑声由谁带来，又究竟为何而来？
lead.warmup: 设想你排了几个小时队，只为看一场免费喜剧，结果节目乏味透顶，登台的演员还大半缺席。就在你满心失望时，报幕员走上台，紧张地站在麦克风前。可他刚一开口，全场却哄堂大笑。他的话究竟哪里出了错，为什么反而成了整晚唯一的亮点？带着这个疑问读课文，看看这场口误到底是怎么发生的。
goals: 能用自己的话复述情节：免费演出、排长队、乏味节目、报幕员口误四条主线。
能正确使用 make a slip of the tongue / make a slip 表达‘口误、失误’。
能区分 must have done / needn't have done / should have done 三种‘对过去’的特殊结构。
能说出 burst out laughing、get round、queue、free、funny 等词在文中的含义与用法。
lead.summary: 课文讲一次免费喜剧演出：消息传开后人们争相排队进场，场内聚了好几百人，可节目乏味至极，许多该登台的演员也没来。整晚唯一令人发笑的是报幕员的开场白——他紧张地站在麦克风前，本想说‘Good evening, ladies and gentlemen’，却把词序说乱，成了‘Good ladies, evening and gentlemen’，于是全场哄堂大笑。
lead.tips: make a slip of the tongue 是固定搭配，表示‘一时口误’；注意 slip 前用 a、tongue 用单数，且常与 make/have 连用，别说成 do a slip。

exercises.q: 汉译英：他紧张时常常口误。
exercises.a: When he is nervous, he often makes a slip of the tongue.
exercises.note: 固定搭配 make a slip of the tongue

exercises.q: 汉译英：消息很快传开了，说市里要上演一场免费演出。
exercises.a: The news soon got round that a free show would be presented in the city.
exercises.note: get round 传开 + 同位语从句

exercises.q: 填空：Those who failed to get in ____ (not feel) disappointed, as many artistes did not come.
exercises.note: needn't have done 本不必做却做了

exercises.q: 句型转换：It is certain that he was very nervous.（用 must 改写为对过去的推测）
exercises.a: He must have been very nervous.
exercises.note: must have done 对过去的推测

exercises.q: 改错：As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out to laugh.
exercises.a: As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out laughing.

exercises.q: 汉译英：报幕员宣布节目开始，但他的话毫无意义。
exercises.a: The advertiser announced the beginning of the programme, but his words made no sense.
exercises.note: announce 宣布；make sense 有意义

exercises.q: 汉译英：他本该早点到，但实际上他迟到了。
exercises.a: He should have arrived earlier, but actually he was late.
exercises.note: should have done 本应做而未做

quiz.q: 课文标题 A Slip of the Tongue 的意思是：
options: 一次成功的演出
一时口误／失言
一张滑倒的纸条
一句逗人的俏皮话
quiz.note: slip 失误 ＋ tongue 舌头＝口误

quiz.q: 下列哪句正确表示‘他紧张时往往会口误’？
options: When he is nervous, he often does a slip of tongue.
When he is nervous, he often makes a slip of the tongue.
When he is nervous, he often makes a slip of tongue.
When he is nervous, he often takes a slip of the tongue.
quiz.note: 固定搭配 make a slip of the tongue，须带 the

quiz.q: ‘消息传开了，说将有一场喜剧演出’应译为：
options: The news got round that a comedy show would be presented.
The news got around to present a comedy show.
The news was got round a comedy show would present.
The news round that a comedy show would be presented.
quiz.note: get round that… 消息传开，that 后为同位语从句

quiz.q: 填空：Those who failed to get in ____ disappointed, as many artistes did not come.
options: needn't have felt
must have felt
should have felt
can't have felt
quiz.note: needn't have done 表本不必做却已做

quiz.q: 填空：As soon as he opened his mouth, everyone burst out ____.
options: to laugh
laughing
laughed
laugh

quiz.q: 下列哪句正确表达‘他本应说 Good evening, ladies and gentlemen，但实际却说错了’？
options: He should say 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', but he said wrong.
He should have said 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', but he actually made a slip.
He must have said 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', but he slip.
He needn't have said 'Good evening, ladies and gentlemen', but he said it.
quiz.note: should have done 表本应做而未做，与 actually 对比
